- [FACT] The ballet Giselle was choreographed by Jean Coralli and Jules Perrot, with a score by Adolphe Adam.
- [FACT] Giselle tells the story of a young peasant girl named Giselle who falls in love with a nobleman named Albrecht.
- [FACT] Albrecht is engaged to another woman, which leads to Giselle dying of a broken heart and becoming a ghostly figure known as a Wilis.
- [FACT] The choreography for Giselle was influenced by classical ballet, folk dances, and court dances.
- [FACT] Giselle is known for its romantic and ethereal quality and has become a beloved classic of the dance repertoire.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Giselle has stood the test of time and remains one of the most important and influential ballets in the history of dance.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The popularity of Giselle is due to its timeless themes of love, betrayal, and redemption, as well as its beautiful and haunting music and choreography.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Notable adaptations include Akram Khan's contemporary version for the English National Ballet, Mats Ek's Giselle with the Royal Swedish Ballet, and Sylvie Guillem's production for Tokyo Ballet.
